summary: Garrett County lookout on Meadow Mountain: a 1921 tower, a 100-foot steel tower dated 1938, restored and open at set times in Deep Creek Lake State Park.

facts.design: 100-foot steel Aermotor tower with a 7 by 7 foot metal cab

access.note: Open on a weekly basis in summer per the register; the Discovery Center says it is only occasionally open for climbing. Contact Deep Creek Lake State Park.

visit.trail_note: Just off Meadow Mountain Trail; climb only when staff have it open

events.note: Lookout tower on the south end of Meadow Mountain, a 47-foot tower near Thayerville; the register counts it among the first lookouts built in Maryland
Moved about a quarter mile southeast to a site with a wider view
Old 47-foot tower dismantled and replaced by an 80-foot steel tower, per a report dated December 13, 1934
Register's build year for the current 100-foot steel tower; not reconciled with the 1934 report
Rebecca Harvey began work as a state lookout here
Last used for fire detection; Harvey's service ended that year
Plaque honoring forest wardens and fire towers installed October 15, 2006

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1921 tower is the earliest one the register and the state report describe here; 1938 is the register's date for the current 100-foot tower. No source read explains the 1934 report of an 80-foot steel tower replacing the 47-foot one, so the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Record height_m 14.3 does not match the register's 100-foot tower (30.5 m); facts.height_m uses the register. Record agency 'Maryland Department of Natural Resources - Forest Service' is not confirmed: the NHLR 'Administered by' value was cut from the fetched text. Registration year: register says April 23, 2007; Discovery Center says 2009. The 1934 replacement and the 1938 build date are not reconciled. Opening hours come from undated pages; check with Deep Creek Lake State Park.
